title: CLEAR Airport Guides: Newark Liberty International Airport
summary: Flying through Newark Liberty International Airport? Discover where to eat, shop, and unwind, plus traveler services and airport tips.
body_markdown:
As one of three major airports serving the New York metropolitan area, Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR) is a key gateway to destinations across the country and around the world. With regional flavors, modern amenities, and convenient transportation connections, EWR offers plenty to discover before your flight.


‍


## **Why Fly Through Newark Liberty International Airport?**


Each of the New York area's three major airports plays a different role. JFK offers the region's broadest selection of long-haul international flights, while LaGuardia is known for its proximity to Manhattan and extensive domestic network. Newark stands out for its direct rail connections and access to both sides of the Hudson, making it a practical choice for business and leisure travelers alike. Newark also combines a strong domestic and international flight network with convenient access to New York City, northern New Jersey, and destinations throughout the Northeast.


In addition, travelers will find a newer airport experience in award-winning Terminal A, with spacious gate areas, intuitive wayfinding, local restaurants, and artwork celebrating New Jersey.


‍


> **Did You Know?** Opened in 1928, Newark Liberty was the first major commercial airport serving the New York metropolitan area and remains one of the country's busiest international gateways.


‍


## **Experience Both Sides of the Hudson at EWR**


Newark Liberty sits where New Jersey and New York meet, giving travelers a taste of both sides of the Hudson before takeoff. From iconic New York flavors to New Jersey businesses and local makers, EWR offers an introduction to the region without leaving the airport.


### **Where to Eat in Newark Airport**


Whether you're craving a legendary New York bagel or discovering a local favorite from across the Hudson, Terminal A offers a preview of the region's culinary scene.


[Ess-a-Bagel](https://www.ess-a-bagel.com/) brings the flavors of the legendary Manhattan bagel shop to EWR, making it an easy choice for a classic New York breakfast before your flight. For something sweet,[Bang Cookies](https://bangcookies.com/) brings its Jersey City roots to the airport with oversized cookies. For a Garden State original,[Jersey Mike's](https://www.jerseymikes.com/1154/newark-nj) traces its roots to a sub shop that opened at the Jersey Shore in 1956.[Carlito's Tacos](https://www.carlitostacos.com/) rounds out the local flavor with inspiration from the diverse communities that shape Newark and northern New Jersey.


### **Where to Shop in Newark Airport**


Terminal A puts New Jersey businesses front and center, giving travelers a chance to discover local products before boarding. Browse[Just Jersey](https://www.justjerseygoods.com/) for locally made gifts, artisan foods, and products celebrating the Garden State. Nearby,[BOLD Newark](https://boldnewark.com/) showcases apparel, accessories, and gifts inspired by Newark's creative community and local entrepreneurs. Together, these locally owned shops offer a distinctly New Jersey alternative to the typical airport gift store and make it easy to bring home a piece of the Garden State.
‍


## **Make the Most of Your Time at Newark**


Whether you're heading across the Hudson, connecting to another flight, or continuing your journey through the Northeast, Newark Liberty offers plenty of ways to spend your time before takeoff. Explore the airport's newest terminal, discover New Jersey art, or take advantage of EWR's rail connections if you have time to venture beyond the airport.


### **Before You Board**


Opened in 2023, Terminal A is more than a place to catch a flight. The terminal celebrates New Jersey's culture and creativity through spacious public areas and[installations from 29 local artists](https://www.newarkairport.com/explore-ewr/terminals/terminal-a/terminal-a-artwork) , with works that reflect the state's history, people, architecture, and character.


Flying through Terminal C? Stop by the[United Centennial exhibit](https://www.newarkairport.com/explore-ewr/terminals/terminal-c) , which celebrates the airline's 100-year history and Newark's role as one of United's most important hubs.


### **If You Have Extra Time**


If you have about an hour before boarding, stay inside the airport and explore beyond your gate. Browse Terminal A's public art, discover locally inspired shops, or grab a bite from a New Jersey or New York favorite. Just be sure to leave enough time to reach your departure gate.


### **Have a Longer Layover?**


Have several hours between flights? Newark Liberty's location gives you options beyond the airport.[AirTrain Newark](https://www.newarkairport.com/transportation/airtrain) connects to Newark Liberty International Airport Station, where you can catch NJ Transit or Amtrak.


For a taste of Newark, head to the[Ironbound District](https://www.newarkhappening.com/things-to-do/ironbound/) , known for its Portuguese, Spanish, and Brazilian restaurants. With enough time, you can also take[NJ Transit](https://www.njtransit.com/destinations/newark-liberty-international-airport) to New York Penn Station and explore Midtown Manhattan. Be sure to allow enough time to return, clear airport security, and reach your gate before boarding.


### **Making a Tight Connection**


If you're connecting through Newark Liberty, confirm your departure gate as soon as you land. AirTrain Newark connects the airport's terminals, but changing terminals may require you to clear airport security again.
‍


## **Plan Ahead at EWR for a Seamless Trip**


Whether you're traveling for business, heading out on vacation, or making a connection, Newark offers services designed to help you navigate the airport with confidence. A little planning before you arrive can help make your trip even more seamless.

### **Accessibility at EWR**


Newark Liberty offers a range of services for travelers with disabilities and additional needs, including wheelchair assistance, accessible transportation, and support for travelers with non-visible disabilities. EWR also participates in the[Hidden Disabilities Sunflower program](https://www.newarkairport.com/explore-ewr/accessibility-services/hidden-disabilities-accessibility) , which allows travelers with non-visible disabilities to discreetly signal that they may need additional time, assistance, or understanding. Free Sunflower lanyards are available in all three terminals.


Terminal A also features two[sensory rooms](https://www.newarkairport.com/explore-ewr/terminals/terminal-a/terminal-a-accessibility-features) , including one before airport security and one after, offering quieter, controlled spaces for travelers who may benefit from a break from the airport environment. Travelers who need mobility assistance or help navigating the airport should arrange support in advance through their airline.


For more information before your trip, explore Newark Liberty's[accessibility services](https://www.newarkairport.com/explore-ewr) for resources covering mobility, transportation, vision, hearing, and non-visible disabilities.
‍


## **Navigate Newark Liberty International Airport**


### **Know Your Terminal**


Newark has three passenger terminals, each serving different airlines and destinations.[Terminal A](https://www.newarkairport.com/explore-ewr/terminals/terminal-a) is home to Air Canada, American Airlines, Delta Air Lines, JetBlue, and select United flights, primarily serving domestic routes.[Terminal B](https://www.newarkairport.com/explore-ewr/terminals/terminal-b) handles most international carriers, including Air France, Lufthansa, Singapore Airlines, TAP Air Portugal, Turkish Airlines, and many others.[Terminal C](https://www.newarkairport.com/explore-ewr/terminals/terminal-c) serves as United Airlines' primary hub, operating hundreds of daily domestic and international flights. Be sure to confirm your departure terminal before leaving for the airport, as gate and terminal assignments can occasionally change. You can find the latest terminal assignments on Newark Liberty's official[airline directory](https://www.newarkairport.com/flights/airlines?utm_source=chatgpt.com) .


### **Get Around with AirTrain**


The free[AirTrain Newark](https://www.newarkairport.com/transportation/airtrain) connects all three terminals, parking garages, rental car facilities, and Newark Liberty International Airport Station. From there, travelers can transfer to[NJ Transit](https://www.njtransit.com/destinations/newark-liberty-international-airport) and[Amtrak](https://www.amtrak.com/stations/ewr) , making Newark one of the easiest airports for exploring the New York City metropolitan area and destinations throughout the Northeast Corridor.

‍


> Traveler Tip: Flying out of Terminal A? The terminal's centralized security checkpoint serves every gate, so once you're through airport security, you can explore the terminal's restaurants, shops, and artwork before making your way to your departure gate.
